### Amos Prays and God Relents
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/amos-prays-and-god-relents
Passage: Amos 7:1-9
Points:
- God showed Amos visions of locusts and fire depicting complete destruction, yet He relented after the prophet interceded.
- Unlike the visions of total devastation, the plumb line signified measuring hearts to separate the unrighteous from the faithful remnant.
- Amos did not plead against the plumb line judgment because distinguishing between covenant-keepers and covenant-breakers reflects God's justice.
- Believers are called to pray with faith that God responds to intercession, even while resting in His sovereign eternal decrees.

### Bible Pathway - Sept. 23, 2012
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-sept-23-2012.html
Passage: Amos 7:8
Points:
- A builder's plumb line tests vertical alignment, showing that Israel had leaned hopelessly off-center and required judgment.
- God's Word functions as our true plumb line, providing an absolute standard to examine our hearts and conduct.
- Without the objective standard of Scripture, human ideas of righteousness become purely subjective and destined to collapse.
- Christ stands in the midst of His people as the true standard, exposing wrongdoing and calling believers to upright obedience.
